selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests a quarter-wave dichroic stack design for longpass filtering: high reflection in 400-700 nm (visible sunlight) and high transmission in 1530-1565 nm (telecom single-photon band). The design draws on recalled thin-film optics principles - alternating high/low index quarter-wave layers centered on the rejection band create a photonic stopband, while wavelengths far from the quarter-wave condition transmit. I would have wanted to look up: exact n/k dispersion curves for HfO2 and SiO2 across 400-1600 nm, typical deposition stress limits for 30-layer stacks, and whether fused silica substrate has a distinct catalog name from SiO2 coating material.

routes.title: Quarter-wave dichroic longpass stack tuned for visible rejection and telecom transmission
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 30-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack centered at 550 nm will produce a high-reflection stopband covering 400-700 nm while transmitting 1530-1565 nm, and individual layer thickness tuning can improve the balance between the two bands without exceeding the 30-layer constraint.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create high reflectance when optical thickness (n×d) equals λ/4 at the design wavelength. The reflection bandwidth scales with the index contrast ratio (nH/nL). Wavelengths significantly longer than the quarter-wave center see reduced optical thickness and transmit. Starting with high-index at the air interface maximizes front-surface reflection contribution.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | fused_silica substrate
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness condition: n×d = λ/4 creates constructive interference for reflected waves at design wavelength
Reflection bandwidth of periodic stack scales with index contrast ratio nH/nL - HfO2/SiO2 provides approximately 1.4:1 contrast in visible
Longpass behavior emerges when quarter-wave center is positioned below the transmission band - wavelengths 2-3× the center wavelength see sub-quarter-wave optical thickness and transmit
Starting stack with high-index layer at air interface increases first-interface Fresnel reflection contribution
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is manufacturable and well-understood in coating practice
30 layers provides sufficient pairs for high visible reflectance while staying within constraint
Thickness tuning allows optimization of edge position between 700 nm and 1530 nm
known_risks: Fused silica substrate name may not resolve - guaranteed_names lists sio2 but substrate may need fused_silica or quartz; this requires catalog lookup to confirm
Refractive index dispersion for HfO2 recalled as ~2.0-2.1 in visible, ~1.9 in near-IR but exact values from dataset may differ and affect quarter-wave calculation
SiO2 index recalled as ~1.45-1.46 across both bands but dispersion slope uncertain
Stress and adhesion for 30-layer stack not modelled - may require lookup of deposition process limits
No angle specified in request - assumed normal incidence but satellite application may have angular spread; this is a hypothesis
Edge steepness between 700 nm and 1530 nm may not be sufficient with simple periodic stack - may need chirp or matching layers not included in this topology
routes.execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer dielectric coating with air incidence on fused_silica substrate. Use exactly 30 layers alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand), starting with hfo2 at the air side. Optimize individual layer thicknesses and the reference quarter-wave center wavelength to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and maximize reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Normal incidence assumed. Both polarization states present but unpolarized weighting. Total layer count fixed at 30. Material names: hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), fused_silica.

valid_candidates should remain above zero across rounds if thickness bounds are physically reasonable
tightest_margin should not systematically decrease - valid designs should remain valid as optimization proceeds
thicknesses_nm should converge to values near quarter-wave condition at reference wavelength with some deviation to balance the two bands
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops to 0 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 20 percent and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.1 for three consecutive rounds, reduce optimization step size and continue
